subject: Private deployment — DPA language and key control questions
messages:
From: Susan Liu <susan.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — DPA language and key control questions

Hi David,

Thanks for running through the initial on‑prem requirements with our infra team last week. Before we move forward with procurement, legal has a few specific DPA / technical questions we need clarified so we can sign off. Can you confirm the following items in writing?

1) Key custody options: we need an explicit description of (a) customer‑managed KMS (BYOK) where keys never leave our HSM, (b) Redwood‑managed keystore with customer key escrow (what triggers escrow release?), and (c) a hybrid where the runtime holds an ephemeral key.

2) Operator access boundaries: what exact access will Redwood engineers/operators have for on‑prem deployments (ability to run commands, pull logs, decrypt payloads, emergency breakglass)? Please call out maximum escalation steps and audit evidence available to AcmeHealth.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: full list of subprocessors for private deployments (incl. cloud partners if any) and whether any telemetry/audit logs may be routed through US/EU/other regions.

4) Data egress triggers: what events cause any outbound traffic (eg. autoscaling, fallback to hosted model, telemetry uploads)? We need guarantees that inference payloads are not sent to hosted Redwood inference endpoints without explicit failover rules.

5) Audit logs / retention: what logs are generated for operator sessions and key operations and how long they are retained? We may require 7 years for certain logs.

I attached a short Q&A doc that legal filled out; answering these will help expedite our DPA addendum review. If it’s easier to do a short call, I can carve out 30m tomorrow afternoon.

Best,

Susan Liu
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
AcmeHealth

Subject: Re: Private deployment — DPA language and key control questions

Susan —

Appreciate the detailed list. Below are concise answers; I’ve attached our latest DPA draft (Redwood_DPA_Draft_v3.pdf) with callouts for the private deployment appendix. If any item needs stronger wording for legal, happy to iterate. We can also do the 30m call — I’m free 11/2pm PT tomorrow.

1) Key custody options
- BYOK (customer KMS): supported. Customer keeps master keys in their HSM/KMS; Redwood runtime integrates via standard KMS APIs (KMIP/Cloud KMS) to perform envelope encryption. Master keys do not leave the customer network; only wrapped data keys are used by the runtime.
- Redwood keystore with escrow: available as an opt‑in addendum. Escrow is strictly time‑bounded and requires either (a) customer‑initiated escrow release via signed request + audit trail, or (b) emergency judicial process. We document exact release flows in Appendix A of the DPA.
- Ephemeral runtime keys: used for cache/worker processes; these keys are generated at runtime and rotate frequently. They are never stored persistently in plaintext.

2) Operator access boundaries
- Default mode: no operator access to customer plaintext data or keys. Operational access is limited to infrastructure‑level troubleshooting (process metrics, container logs).
- Breakglass: we support a documented breakglass workflow requiring dual approval (CS + security), time‑limited session elevation, and full session recording. All breakglass actions produce tamper‑evident audit logs that are exported to the customer SIEM.
- Support tools: remote sessions are via bastion with timeboxed credentials and recorded terminal and file transfer logs; we can provide read‑only proxies for query inspection when requested.

3) Subprocessors & transfers
- For private/VPC/on‑prem deployments, subprocessors are limited: orchestration partners, secure transport/CDN for initial software delivery, and designated hardware vendors. We will enumerate the names in the DPA addendum table and commit to notify AcmeHealth for any changes 30 days in advance.
- Telemetry: runtime heartbeat and anonymized telemetry are disabled by default for private installations. Any telemetry sent (if enabled) is configurable by tenant and can be restricted to specific regions.

4) Data egress triggers
- No inference payload is sent to hosted Redwood endpoints unless you explicitly opt into cross‑tenant failover or we mutually agree on emergency fallback.
- Autoscaling within a private cluster is local, and burst to hosted capacity is only possible when explicitly configured and signed off in the SLA.

5) Audit logs / retention
- Operator session logs, key operation records, and administrative actions are recorded. Retention is configurable per customer; standard options include 90 days, 1 year, or custom (we can support 7 years via archive exports to your storage).

Next steps: I’ll loop in engineering (Rishi) to provide a short technical appendix on how wrapped keys and HSM integration look in practice. If that sounds good, I’ll send an updated DPA with the private appendices integrated and a DocuSign envelope.

Thanks,

David Kim
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Draft_v3.pdf

Following up with the engineering appendix Susan requested — high level technical notes to include in the addendum:

- Integration model: we support both networked KMS (TLS‑mutual auth) and in‑box HSM connectors. In the networked KMS case, only wrapped data keys are persisted on Redwood nodes; master key operations (sign/decrypt) are proxied to the customer KMS over an authenticated channel.

- Plaintext handling: plaintext never lands on persistent disk. Memory is protected and scrubbed after use; core dumps are disabled in production builds.

- HSM / KMS attestations: we can provide attestation artifacts (SPC reports/HSM vendor audit snapshot) as part of the onboarding package.

- Operator workflows: operators can trigger pre‑approved maintenance flows (log collection, process restart) but cannot export key material. Breakglass sessions require an out‑of‑band token + justification and are recorded.

- Telemetry & logs: operational telemetry is metric‑only by default (latency, queue depth). We will expose per‑tenant toggles to disable even metric collection. Audit logs for admin actions include timestamp, actor id, justification, and session recording id. Export formats: syslog, JSON over HTTPS, or S3 archive.

If legal needs specific machine‑readable examples (sample audit log entries, sample KMS API calls) I can paste those into the addendum — I’ll prepare a 1‑page snippet for the DPA.

-rishi

- Escrow remains an opt‑in addendum; we require the escrow release flow to include dual approval and customer notification window — language in Appendix A is sufficient with a minor clarifying sentence (attached).
- Breakglass is acceptable provided session recordings and export to our SIEM are immediate.
